conviction_note: Six of seven prior reactions were up at a 13.43% median including +36.48% last quarter, and a third-party figure in the capture puts the implied move near 12%, so the distribution is wide and historically right-skewed; I tilt only modestly negative because the corpus supplies a live precedent - a directly comparable consumption-software name that grew 36% and raised guidance and still fell 17% - against a stock 9.35% off its high after a 152% run, with bearish option flow and an executive sale documented in the run-in.

findings.finding: The governing precedent for a high-multiple consumption-software print in this tape is captured in the same sweep as the SNOW preview material: Datadog reported Q2 2026 revenue up 36% and raised guidance, and the stock fell 17% - and it arrives alongside evidence that Snowflake's own pre-print positioning is defensive (increased bearish options activity ahead of earnings, an 'eye-catching' executive stock sale, and coverage asking what short sellers are betting against after a near-50% year) while the sell-side has stretched targets to $405 (Cantor, +44%) and $677, and the stock sits only 9.35% below its high after rising 152.53% off its low.
findings.corpus_ref: snapshots/20260901T153017Z.json - the Datadog piece, plus https://www.gurufocus.com/news/2787441/snowflake-snow-sees-increased-bearish-options-activity-ahead-of-earnings-snow-stock-news, https://www.tipranks.com/news/insider-trading/top-snowflake-executive-makes-eye-catching-move-with-insider-stock-sale-insider-trading-news, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/snowflake-nearly-50-2026-short-134000649.html, https://moneycheck.com/snowflake-snow-stock-price-target-jumps-to-405-as-cantor-fitzgerald-boosts-forecast-44 and https://www.saastr.com/the-saas-rout-of-2026-is-even-worse-than-you-think-for-the-first-time-ever-software-now-trades-at-a-discount-to-the-sp-500/
findings.why_not_priced: Every preview document in this capture frames the question as whether Snowflake beats - 'watch these 3 numbers', 'here's what to expect', 'buy, sell or hold before Q2'. None of them frames it as whether beating is sufficient, even though the corpus contains the answer from a peer three weeks earlier: 36% growth plus a raised guide produced minus 17%. The regime datapoint sits beside it - software trading at a discount to the S&P 500 for the first time ever - and Snowflake is the sector's winner rather than its victim, up 152.53% off the low and 9.35% off the high, which is exactly the position from which a good print gets sold. The corroborating positioning evidence points the same way and is not aggregated anywhere: bearish option flow, an executive sale, and a documented short-seller thesis after a near-50% year. I keep the number to about a seventh of the median because I am arguing against a 6-of-7 up record and because the corpus is equally clear that software can rip - Atlassian +34%, Twilio +27%, Cloudflare +9% in one surge, with Gartner revising 2026 software spend up to 15.1% growth.
findings.independence: This is one finding assembled from a source cluster, not several, and I am saying so: the Datadog piece, the gurufocus options piece, the tipranks insider piece, the Yahoo short-seller piece and the saastr regime piece are five different publishers but they collapse to a single argument about the bar. The only genuinely separate datapoint pulling the other way is https://www.snowflake.com/en/news/press-releases/snowflake-expands-aws-collaboration-with-6b-commitment-to-accelerate-enterprise-agentic-ai-adoption/, which is a company source but dated 2026-05-27 alongside the last print and therefore priced.

searched_and_found_nothing: an unpriced read on the $6bn AWS commitment: the press release and the TechCrunch write-up are both dated 2026-05-27, the day of the Q1 FY27 print that produced +36.48%, so it is in the price

a consumption-model inversion I could sign: Snowflake launched a Cortex AI Gateway explicitly 'to control AI agents and prevent runaway enterprise costs', which for a consumption-priced vendor cuts both ways - it removes an adoption blocker and it hands customers a spend brake - and I could not resolve the direction, so I left it out
the size of the executive stock sale, which reaches the corpus only as a tipranks headline with no body and no matching Form 4 detail

a measured option-implied move: the only figure is in a skipped URL slug, https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/snowflake-options-indicate-12-move-on-sept-2-earnings-93CH-4877502, which I used to sanity-check the 13.43% baseline median rather than to set anything
short-interest figures from a primary source: every fintel.io URL failed to fetch
a product-revenue or net-revenue-retention datapoint newer than Q1 FY27's 126%
baseline_tension: It cuts against the reaction history hard - six of seven up, last print +36.48% - and sits mildly with the run-up, which is -3.02% over five days and -3.47% over twenty. That disagreement with the base rate is why the magnitude is small relative to the 13.43% median and why the upside band is wide.
corpus_limits: Two documents are tripwire-flagged and I did not use either occurrence: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/25/snowflake-stock-fans-should-prepare-for-september-2-as-ai-agents-are-pouring-more-data-into-it/ (appearing twice in snapshots/20260831T154457Z.json). No option chain or skew, so the 12% figure is snippet-grade. Numerous URLs failed to fetch and exist only as headlines, including every short-interest page, the investing.com implied-move piece and the tipranks insider-sale piece, so the positioning half of the finding is headline-grade rather than measured. Doc bodies are single-line HTML dumps read by pattern window rather than in full. This is an amc print, so the 2026-09-02T15:19:12Z sweep is pre-release and admissible.
